title: Sell Mineral Rights in Alcova, WY
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Alcova, WY | Natrona County
metaDescription: Alcova, WY sits southwest of the old Salt Creek oil field trend in Natrona County. Get a plain-spoken read on what your mineral interest is actually worth.
heroLead: Alcova is a small reservoir community southwest of Casper, and the mineral interests I see out here are almost always small legacy fractions off old Natrona County ranch land, not active production.
intro: Natrona County built its reputation on the Salt Creek field north of Casper, one of the largest oil discoveries in the country when it came in over a century ago, but Alcova itself sits well outside that trend, closer to the North Platte River canyon and the reservoir. Most of what's recorded down here is undeveloped or long-dormant mineral acreage tied to homestead-era patents.

If a deed turned up in a family estate with an Alcova or Pathfinder Reservoir legal description, I can tell you within a day or two whether it's ever been leased and what a realistic number looks like.

sections.heading: Why this ground is quiet
paragraphs: The productive trend that made Natrona County famous runs north of Casper, not southwest toward the reservoir. Alcova-area minerals mostly sit outside any active spacing unit, which is exactly why courthouse records show old leases from decades back that simply expired without a well ever being drilled.

That doesn't mean the interest is worthless. It means it prices as undeveloped acreage with basin-adjacent potential, not as a royalty-producing asset, and I'll be direct with you about which category yours falls into.

sections.heading: Confirming what you actually own
paragraphs: A lot of Alcova-area deeds I run into describe fractional interests in quarter sections that trace back to a single original homestead, split across heirs for three or four generations. Before I quote anything, I pull the Natrona County recorder's chain of title myself so you know exactly what percentage of what acreage you're holding.

Sometimes the paperwork is straightforward, a single deed transferring a clean fraction. Other times I find a tangle of quitclaims and old mortgage releases that need sorting before the actual ownership picture is clear. Either way, I do that work before you have to spend a dollar on an attorney.

faqs.question: Has anyone drilled near Alcova?
faqs.answer: Not in recent history, in most sections. Activity in Natrona County has stayed concentrated closer to Casper and the Salt Creek trend. I'll check your specific legal description before saying anything definitive.

faqs.question: Is my interest worth selling if nothing's producing?
faqs.answer: Undeveloped interest still has a value, just priced lower than producing acreage. I'll give you a range based on comparable Natrona County trades.

faqs.question: How do I even find my legal description?
faqs.answer: Send me the deed or probate paperwork you have, even a partial copy, and I'll match it against the county plat myself.

faqs.question: What if my interest is shared with siblings or cousins?
faqs.answer: That's common with reservoir-area ranch land. I'll quote your individual share and can coordinate with co-owners if the whole family wants to sell together.
